executive_summary:
The codebase scores **A (91.7/100)** across 209 files — no critical defects, zero import cycles, and average cyclomatic complexity of 4.2. That headline is accurate but incomplete. Underneath it, **coupling collapsed 19 points** (100 → 81) between Apr 22 and May 13, the single largest metric movement in the observation window and the only reading that crossed the 5-point inflection threshold. This happened for a legitimate reason — Phases A–D wired `user_id` isolation across every domain table, added `forUser` wrappers, HMAC OAuth state, encrypted vault helpers, and webhook-to-user mapping — but the structural cost is now visible: `auth.ts` has 31 fan-in callers, `connection.ts` has 17, and both have become de facto chokepoints that every new route touches by default.

Trajectory is mixed. Complexity is improving (+3 pts net), cohesion hit a perfect 100 after the db.ts domain-module split, and TDG is marginally up. Duplication is the one dimension actively trending the wrong direction: it fell 5 points from baseline (96 → 91) and has not recovered, with 77 clone groups and 999 duplicate lines spread across chart cards, the three `LogsTable` variants, and self-clones inside `connection.ts`, `logs.ts`, and `upsert.ts`. Self-clones — where the same block is duplicated within a single file — are the most urgent duplication risk because both copies must be updated simultaneously on the next edit.

The three concrete risks are: (1) **auth.ts as a single structural chokepoint** — 31 dependents, highest betweenness in the graph, and a breaking change here disconnects more module pairs than any other file; (2) **the coach subsystem god-route** — `api/chat/route.ts` scores 0.985 on the hotspot index (18 commits, 98th-percentile complexity) while still owning SSE transport, agentic loop orchestration, tool dispatch, and persistence in one handler; (3) **`connection.ts` absorbing every schema change** — 24 commits, the single D-grade file in the repo (TDG 62.7), cyclomatic complexity 46, and 16.7% internal duplication.

The path forward is three targeted refactors, not a broad cleanup. Split `auth.ts` into session/guard/identity submodules to reduce its blast radius. Finish the coach route split that PR #675e0d4 started — push loop orchestration into `loop.ts` and persistence into `persistence.ts`, leaving `route.ts` as pure SSE transport. Extract a migration runner from `connection.ts` so schema changes stop touching live connection code. Beyond those three, the highest-value quick wins are extracting a `LogsTable` base component (eliminates ~150 lines), a shared `useChartDateRange()` hook (eliminates ~74 lines), and a `signAppleJWT()` helper from the auth/push duplication (eliminates ~18 lines but closes a security-relevant divergence risk).
key_findings: **Coupling (score 81, -19 pts from baseline)** — Only metric that crossed the inflection threshold. `auth.ts` fan-in reached 31 (threshold 20), `connection.ts` fan-in is 17. Driven by Phases A–D adding cross-module wiring. No cycles exist (cycle_count: 0), which is the one bright spot. See `components.json` coupling section.

**God-route hotspot** — `apps/web/src/app/api/chat/route.ts` scores 0.985 (max is 1.0), churned 18 times in 12 days, sits at 98th-percentile complexity. Handles SSE keepalive, agentic loop, tool dispatch, and chat persistence in one file. PR #675e0d4 started a split that stalled. Finish it. See `hotspots.json`.

**`connection.ts` is the only D-grade file** — TDG score 62.7, cyclomatic complexity 46, nesting 6 levels, 16.7% internal duplication, 24 commits. It is simultaneously the worst-structured and most-churned file in the repo. Extract a migrations runner; freeze the connection interface. See `tdg.json` and `hotspots.json`.

**Self-clones inside single files** — `logs.ts` has an identical 15-line block at lines 80–94 and 196–210. `connection.ts` has an exact 11-line block at lines 460–470 and 472–482. `upsert.ts` has 3 near-identical 13–14 line blocks. These will silently diverge on the next edit because only one copy gets updated. Fix these before any other duplication work. See `duplication.json`.

**Apple JWT clone is a security-relevant divergence** — `apple-web.ts` (auth) and `apns.ts` (push) share an 82%-similar 18–22 line JWT signing block (group 14 in duplication report). Any key rotation or algorithm fix applied to one will be missed in the other. Extract `signAppleJWT()` to `src/lib/apple/jwt.ts`. See `duplication.json`.

**Phase D cutover debt still live** — Three coordinated TODOs across `token.ts` (lines 25, 90) and `auth.ts` (line 187) mark a `tokens.json` fallback that is still active for `userId===1`. Missing any one of the three on removal leaves the legacy path half-alive. Track as a single atomic task. See `satd.json`.

**`sync.test.ts` appears as an isolated node** — The test file exists but has no outgoing imports, suggesting it is empty or a stub. `sync.ts` is 677 lines, the most operationally critical path (all data ingestion), and currently has no effective test coverage. See `graph.json`.

**`useChatSend.ts` has the highest raw cyclomatic complexity in the codebase** — Score 61 (C+ grade), 415 lines, sole owner. Handles optimistic UI, SSE stream parsing, and retry logic in one hook. Extract `useSSEStream` and a retry utility. See `tdg.json` and `ownership.json`.

**`TopBar.tsx` ↔ `db.ts` co-change strength 0.75** — A UI chrome component co-changes with the DB layer on 6 of 8 commits. There is no valid import reason for this coupling. A shared data-shape or auth assumption is leaking into presentation. Identify the implicit dependency and make it explicit. See `temporal.json`.

high_priority.title: Split auth.ts to reduce 31-dependent blast radius
high_priority.description: Extract `getCurrentUser()` (session token → user ID) into `lib/auth/session.ts`. Push cookie manipulation into `lib/auth/cookies.ts` (already exists at fan-in 6). Leave only orchestration glue in `auth.ts`. This is the file with the highest betweenness in the entire graph — a breaking change here disconnects more module pairs than any other single edit. Target: fan-in below 20, matching the hub threshold.

high_priority.title: Finish the coach route split (api/chat/route.ts, hotspot score 0.985)
high_priority.description: PR #675e0d4 started this but stalled. `route.ts` should own only SSE transport and request parsing. Move loop orchestration fully into `loop.ts` (define a `LoopContext` interface to decouple it from the transport). Move persistence calls into `persistence.ts`. `tools.ts` should be split by domain: `toolsSleep.ts`, `toolsWorkout.ts`, `toolsRecovery.ts`, re-exported from an index. This directly addresses the highest-scoring hotspot and the most churn-concentrated subsystem.

high_priority.title: Extract migration runner from connection.ts (only D-grade file, TDG 62.7)
high_priority.description: `connection.ts` is 686 lines with complexity 46 and absorbs every schema change across 24 commits. Split into: `connection.ts` (connection factory + pool only, frozen interface), `migrations.ts` (schema initialization and migration runner), and `wal.ts` (WAL/pragma config). After the split, freeze `connection.ts` as a no-logic boundary — no new code should ever be added here beyond connection setup.

high_priority.title: Fix self-clones in logs.ts, connection.ts, and upsert.ts before next edit
high_priority.description: Three files have exact duplicates within themselves. `logs.ts` lines 80–94 and 196–210 are identical (15 lines). `connection.ts` lines 460–470 and 472–482 are identical (11 lines). `upsert.ts` has three near-identical 13–14 line upsert blocks. These will silently diverge on the next edit because only the visible copy gets updated. Fix as local helper functions before any other duplication work.

high_priority.title: Consolidate Apple JWT signing (auth/push divergence risk)
high_priority.description: `apps/web/src/lib/auth/apple-web.ts` and `apps/web/src/lib/push/apns.ts` share an 82%-similar JWT signing block. Any key rotation or signing algorithm fix applied to one file will be missed in the other. Extract `signAppleJWT(privateKey, teamId, keyId)` to `src/lib/apple/jwt.ts` and import from both callsites. Small change, high-consequence risk if left.

high_priority.title: Write real tests for sync.ts — sync.test.ts is currently a stub
high_priority.description: `sync.ts` is 677 lines, the most operationally critical path in the codebase (all WHOOP data ingestion), and `sync.test.ts` appears as an isolated node in the dependency graph with no outgoing imports — meaning it imports nothing and tests nothing. Any breakage in `sync.ts` silently stops all data ingestion. Add at minimum: happy-path upsert test, cooldown logic test, abort-after-commit test.

high_priority.title: Remove Phase D cutover debt atomically (three locations)
high_priority.description: The `tokens.json` fallback for `userId===1` is still live code across three coordinated points: `token.ts` line 25 (saveTokens), `token.ts` line 90 (loadTokens), and `auth.ts` line 187. Missing any one leaves the legacy path half-alive. Add a grep guard or shared `PHASE_D_COMPLETE` constant so removal is atomic. Track as a single issue tied to the Phase D milestone.

medium_priority.title: Extract LogsTable base component (~150 lines eliminated)
medium_priority.description: `ChatLogsTable`, `RouteLogsTable`, and `SyncLogsTable` are the same table rendered with different columns — 67 duplicate lines each across groups 7, 18, 21, and 30 in the duplication report. Extract a `LogsTable` base component to `src/app/(dashboard)/logs/LogsTable.tsx` parameterized by column config. Biggest single duplication win in the codebase by lines saved.

medium_priority.title: Extract shared chart card hook (~74 lines eliminated)
medium_priority.description: `BedtimePatternsCard`, `NapCalendar`, `NapTrackerCard`, `RecoveryReboundCard`, and `SleepConsistencyCard` all contain identical 18–20 line date-range boilerplate (group 26). Extract `useChartDateRange()` to `src/components/charts/shared/`. Also address `HRVTrend.tsx` ↔ `TrendChart.tsx` which share 57 duplicate lines across three groups — merge the 40-line core chart rendering logic into a single parameterized component.

medium_priority.title: Consolidate whoop/ module shared assumptions into WhoopSession struct
medium_priority.description: `client.ts` ↔ `token.ts` ↔ `upsert.ts` form a tight co-change group (temporal coupling strength 0.67) because they share implicit assumptions about token shape and refresh behavior. Extract a `WhoopSession` or `WhoopConfig` type (token, expiry, userId) passed explicitly so a token-format change touches one definition. This directly addresses the strongest temporal coupling cluster outside the DB layer.

medium_priority.title: Extract shared DB query helpers (~71 lines eliminated)
medium_priority.description: Groups 1, 5, 6, and 17 in the duplication report show repeated query patterns across `recovery.ts`, `sleep.ts`, `strain.ts`, `devices.ts`, `integrations.ts`, `coach.ts`, and `webhook.ts`. Extract `fetchDomainRows()` and owner-scoped query helpers to `src/lib/db/shared.ts`. Also extract the internal webhook handler pattern — `webhook.ts` clones the same block 3 times internally (group 6), which is the highest fix-one-miss-others risk.

medium_priority.title: Investigate TopBar.tsx ↔ db.ts temporal coupling (strength 0.75)
medium_priority.description: A UI chrome component co-changes with the database layer on 6 of 8 commits. There is no valid import relationship. Identify what implicit data-shape or auth assumption TopBar is reacting to and make it explicit — either a dedicated query hook or a server component prop. Left unaddressed, every DB schema change will continue to pull TopBar into the same PR.

medium_priority.title: Split upsert.ts into per-resource modules
medium_priority.description: `upsert.ts` is 502 lines at 95th-percentile complexity (hotspot score 0.924) handling workouts, sleep, recovery, and cycles in one file. Split into `upsertSleep.ts`, `upsertWorkout.ts`, `upsertRecovery.ts`, and `upsertHelpers.ts`. This also fixes the three near-identical internal clone blocks (group 15 in duplication report) naturally.

medium_priority.title: Document crypto/vault.ts encryption format and key derivation
medium_priority.description: `vault.ts` is 111 lines, sole owner. It holds the encryption key derivation and vault format for all stored WHOOP tokens and credentials. Any format change without a documented migration path would corrupt all stored credentials silently. Add inline comments defining the vault wire format, key derivation inputs, and migration procedure.

ongoing.title: Protect auth.ts as a frozen interface during Phase E+
ongoing.description: auth.ts has the highest betweenness of any non-sink node in the graph. Until the split is complete, treat it as a protected file: any PR touching auth.ts should explicitly verify the existing auth.test.ts suite passes and document which of the 31 dependents were tested.

ongoing.title: Keep connection.ts as a no-logic boundary post-refactor
ongoing.description: After extracting the migration runner, enforce that no new logic is added to connection.ts. It should contain only: connection factory, pool config, and WAL pragma setup. Any schema-related change goes into migrations.ts. This is the only way to stop it re-accumulating the 24-commit churn pattern.

ongoing.title: Add inline documentation to high-context files before starting Phase E
ongoing.description: Bus factor is 1 across all 208 files. The highest re-entry risk files (those that are large, complex, and stateful) need inline documentation before extending them further. Priority order: `connection.ts` (686 lines, schema migration assumptions), `sync.ts` (677 lines, retry/upsert flow), `coach/tools.ts` (555 lines, AI tool definitions and query shapes), `upsert.ts` (502 lines, entity upsert invariants), `crypto/vault.ts` (encryption format), `lib/illness.ts` (detection thresholds and heuristics).

ongoing.title: Watch coupling score — halt new cross-module wiring if it falls below 75
ongoing.description: Coupling dropped from 100 to 81 in three weeks of foundation work. The Phase D build was legitimate, but the trajectory (slope -9.5/period, r=0.99) means two more similar sprints would push it below 60. Before starting any Phase E feature that adds new API routes or auth flows, check whether it can reuse an existing import path rather than adding a new one.

ongoing.title: Extract test DB mock fixture to src/test-utils/dbMocks.ts
ongoing.description: Six test files share a 9–16 line mock/setup block at 90% similarity (group 13 in duplication report). Without a shared fixture, every new test file will copy this block again. Low-effort extraction, but without it the pattern compounds with every new test added.

ongoing.title: Convert smoke-phase-a.ts and smoke-phase-c.ts to proper test suite
ongoing.description: Both scripts have the highest raw cyclomatic complexity in the entire codebase (23.0 and 24.0 respectively) for what are ostensibly one-off smoke scripts. They contain real business logic and integration coverage that is currently invisible to the test runner. Convert to `tests/integration/` and add to CI.

ongoing.title: Rename SECURITY marker in tests/test_integrations.py line 267 to INVARIANT
ongoing.description: The marker is a test docstring asserting that save_tokens never writes plaintext credentials. It is correct and protective, not a vulnerability. Renaming it prevents false positives in any future automated SATD/security scans that treat all SECURITY markers as issues.
